title: Improved H 2  storage performance in hydride perovskite Mg 2 FeH 6  by substitution of Mg with Be
content: In this work, we provide theoretical insights into improved H2 storage performance in vacancy-ordered double perovskite-type hydride Mg2FeH6 by substitution of Mg with Be. Electronic structure calculations predict that the cubic Mg2FeH6 and MgBeFeH6 are semiconductors with direct band gaps of 1.90 and 1.85 eV at X point coinciding with chemical bonding analysis. By investigating geometric factors, elastic constants and self-consistent phonon calculations, we find that Mg2FeH6 and MgBeFeH6 are dynamically and mechanically stable in cubic phase at finite temperatures, satisfying Born's stability criteria. Our calculations predict that by Be substitution, theoretical gravimetric (volumetric) H2 storage capacity is increased to 6.30 wt% (181.52 g L−1) showing a rise of 16%, and the DFT-calculated dehydrogenation temperature is reduced to 403.81 K considering zero-point energy by quantum effect. Furthermore, nudged elastic band calculation indicates that activation energy for H migration is much reduced from 0.99 to 0.36 eV in MgBeFeH6 by partial substitution of Mg with Be. The improved performance is ascribed to weakened chemical bonding by partial substitution of Mg with Be in cubic MgBeFeH6. Our work highlights that MgBeFeH6 can be a potential H2 storage material due to its high H2 storage capacity, mechanical and dynamical stabilities, suitable dehydrogenation temperature and improved kinetic properties.
